LRHC-1.label: proposed_not_promoted
LRHC-1.rationale: Real-estate brokerage is the most aggressively-regulated 'agent count' claim in any domain — every salesperson must hold an active state license affiliated with one and only one broker. Filing claims 2,769 licensees, of which the bulk should be FL-licensed under 'La Rosa Realty'. State public lookup is the canonical adjudicator. Each licensee is publicly addressable.
LRHC-1.endpoint: Per-state: Florida DBPR (https://www.myfloridalicense.com/wl11.asp), Texas TREC (https://www.trec.texas.gov/apps/license-holder-search/), California DRE (https://www.dre.ca.gov/PublicASP/pplinfo.asp), Georgia GREC (https://grec.state.ga.us/grec-search/), North Carolina NCREC (https://www.ncrec.gov/RecsearchOnline.aspx), Puerto Rico DACO. Affiliated-licensee endpoints typically return list of license holders with status, expiration, and primary broker.
LRHC-1.note: score UNVERIFIABLE; connector not yet built

LRHC-2.label: proposed_not_promoted
LRHC-2.rationale: Every brokerage office must be licensed as a branch with its supervising broker registered. State office count = ground truth on the 26-office claim. The same registry corroborates address (matches Item 2 of 10-K) and supervising-broker continuity.
LRHC-2.endpoint: FL DBPR Real Estate (Bureau of Education and Testing) — searches BrokerOffice; TX TREC Branch Office Search; CA DRE Branch Office Search; GA GREC office registry; NC NCREC Firm Office Search
LRHC-2.note: score UNVERIFIABLE; connector not yet built

creative_extensions.rationale: Florida is the corporate HQ and the documented majority of offices (Celebration, Kissimmee, Davenport, Jacksonville, Miami, etc.) — FL DBPR should show the lion's share of the 2,769 licensees if the count is real
